tfn.s: Maricarmen lived in her flat for more than seventy years.
tfn.why: The text says she lived in the same flat "for more than 70 years".

tfn.s: No police came to the building on 23 September.
tfn.why: The text says "police arrived to carry out the eviction".

tfn.s: Maricarmen died less than a month after the eviction.
tfn.why: She was evicted on 23 September and died on 7 October, about two weeks later.

tfn.s: The text says the eviction was shown to be the cause of her death.
tfn.why: It says the eviction "has not been shown to be the cause of her death".

tfn.s: The new owners wanted to turn the building into a hotel.

tfn.s: Abascal died fewer than three weeks after the eviction.
tfn.why: The eviction took place on 23 September and she died on 7 October, a gap of two weeks.

tfn.s: The text treats the claim that the eviction killed her as proven.
tfn.why: It says that attributing her death to the eviction "would go beyond the available medical evidence".

tfn.s: The campaigners received legal help from a tenants' union.
tfn.why: The text does not say who, if anyone, helped them legally.

tfn.s: The writer suggests that holiday lets are not the only reason for the shortage of long-term rentals.
tfn.why: The text names demand, limited supply and investor interest too, and says the impact of holiday lets "varies by location".

tfn.s: Tenant organisations and property owners both urge tighter regulation.
tfn.why: Tenant groups want stronger regulation, but owners warn that "excessive restrictions" may reduce the incentive to rent.

speak.title: Role-play: a rent rise
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: You own a flat and your costs have gone up. You want to raise the rent by 10% from next month. Explain why. You can agree to a smaller rise if the tenant offers a longer contract.

b.text: You've lived in your flat for six years and you love the area. Your landlord wants a rent rise that you can't afford. Ask for time and a fair deal, and say what you can offer.

phrases: I'd like to talk about the rent.
I've lived here for six years.
I'm afraid I can't afford that.
Would you consider a smaller rise?
We're willing to sign a longer contract.
That's fair, so let's agree on it.
speak.after: Tell the class what you agreed and whether both sides were happy.
